markdown_report:
**Recommendation:** complete the endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff experiment before adding architecture. At 30% progress, this offers the clearest feasible comparison against the supplied uniform control; validation improvement remains unproven.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, terminal masking matches appended-MASK inference. Strictly truncated prefixes prevent bidirectional target leakage. Second, separately normalized reconstruction and terminal losses preserve explicit objective weights. Example counts alone cannot establish gradient allocation. Third, recent-cutoff sampling targets stale-interest influence and broad historical affinity displacing current choices. It cannot identify fulfilled needs or compatibility.

**Insights from related work.** BERT4Rec establishes masked-item learning [1]. Adding terminal supervision alone therefore offers limited originality. TiSASRec supports learning historical interval effects [2]. Transferring these effects into BERT4Rec requires a defined MASK relation without an unknown next-event timestamp. MARS motivates attribute-sensitive matching [3]. Its pretrained setting provides limited evidence for a text encoder trained from scratch here.

The diagnostics favor a controlled sampling test: Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific have weaker lower-tail margins, 0.5434 and 0.624, despite generally healthy sampled separation. These are training probes, not HR@10. Fixed 64/64 allocation snapshots conflict with Bernoulli-allocation definitions; reconcile documentation before attributing effects.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed atomic experiment | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target exposure | BERT4Rec masking [1] | Recent nonterminal cutoffs | Target frequency and context length also change |
| Temporal representation | Historical interval attention [2] | Log-gap attention bias | MASK temporal semantics |
| Content specificity | Attribute matching [3] | Joint title-token embedding gate | Sparse supervision without pretraining |

Scores below use **O** originality, **F** future potential, **U** user alignment, **M** model alignment, **D** implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell gives a positive and negative rationale.

| Idea | O | F | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recent cutoffs | 3: precise ablation; established ingredients | 7: interpretable foundation; context confounding | 8: current intent; no compatibility inference | 7: terminal discrimination; mixed probes | 3: sampler change; careful counters |
| Historical-gap bias | 5: family adaptation; established mechanism | 7: adaptive persistence; timestamp sensitivity | 8: stale interests; recent need uncertain | 6: contextual separation; no causal evidence | 6: small bias tables; adapter changes |
| Title-token gate | 4: joint lightweight encoder; established fusion | 7: specific content; sparse text learning | 8: specificity; similarity misses complements | 5: discrimination hypothesis; unmeasured mechanism | 6: one network; vocabulary and writer changes |

**Selected algorithm.** Keep reconstruction unchanged and terminal endpoint probability at 0.1. Conditional on a nonterminal target, sample equally from all eligible positions and their latest ten. Optimize `0.5 * mean_reconstruction_CE + 0.5 * mean_terminal_CE` in one BERT4Rec.

This explicitly targets two user failures—older interests receiving excessive influence and broad affinity displacing current intent—and the model’s weaker lower-tail separation. Measure terminal margins separately; select solely through pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve fixed seeds, routing, budgets, checkpoint selection, and one checkpoint per category. Keep appended-MASK inference and maximum-nonpadding readout unchanged. No gain or causal attribution is established by the supplied evidence.

idea.description: Complete the controlled endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff treatment against the supplied uniform-cutoff BERT4Rec control. Change only the conditional distribution of nonterminal terminal-mask targets; train one independent model per category and deploy one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The proposal addresses stale historical influence and broadly related recommendations displacing specific current interests. Reconstruction retains supervision for enduring interests while recent-prefix terminal targets emphasize observed next choices. Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific have comparatively weak lower-tail sampled margins, motivating a terminal-discrimination experiment without assuming representation collapse. Current diagnostics do not establish that this treatment improves HR@10, compatibility, or fulfilled-demand recognition.
idea.implementation_notes:
Apply this sampler to the supplied corrected BERT4Rec rather than reconstructing an unavailable training script. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Preserve the control's architecture, optimizer, full-real-item tied-head cross-entropy, reconstruction corruption, 64 reconstruction plus 64 terminal sequences per batch, validation cadence, and earliest-best checkpoint selection. Each branch contributes half of its independently target-normalized loss. Do not change to Bernoulli branch allocation: reconcile the conflicting diagnostic definition with measured sampler behavior and write accurate definitions.

Use independent purpose-specific data RNG streams following the supplied SeedSequence scheme. The same cutoff uniform maps through the two policies' inverse CDFs. Preserve all other generators and tensor shapes where feasible. For n >= 3, the final training target retains probability 0.1; n == 2 is an explicit endpoint exception. Target recency refers to event position, not elapsed time. Record cutoff status, selected-target probabilities, context lengths, target item frequencies, valid branch targets, and detached loss sums. The experiment measures a total sampling-policy effect, including context-length and item-exposure changes.

Keep one jointly trained BERT4Rec and one selected checkpoint per category; never combine experimental arms. Preserve the embedded predictor writer and checkpoint format because architecture and inference do not change. At inference append the reserved MASK after at most L-1 observed items, left-pad, and read the maximum nonpadding index. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), and the actual trained view.model.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Keep B x L loader tensors and distinguish measured terminal probes from reconstruction probes explicitly. Unmatched bookkeeping must remain unavailable; final-position coverage cannot identify branch allocation. Evaluate only with the unchanged host protocol and select by macro validation HR@10. All trials and diagnostics count against 43,200 GPU seconds. Use supplied histories only for this intervention; unavailable attributes and simulator traits provide no supervision.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

CATEGORIES = ('Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
              'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl')

def choose_terminal_target(n, u, recent=True):
    """Zero-based target index and its probability; u is uniform in [0, 1)."""
    if n < 2:
        return None, 0.0
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 1.0
    if u < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 0.1
    m = n - 2  # nonterminal indices 1, ..., n-2
    p = np.full(m, 1.0 / m, dtype=np.float64)
    if recent:
        k = min(10, m)
        p *= 0.5
        p[-k:] += 0.5 / k
    cdf = np.cumsum(p)
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    v = (u - 0.1) / 0.9
    j = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')), m - 1)
    return j + 1, float(0.9 * p[j])

def terminal_example(history, u, maxlen, mask_id, recent=True):
    assert maxlen >= 2
    t, probability = choose_terminal_target(len(history), u, recent)
    if t is None:
        return None
    context = history[max(0, t - (maxlen - 1)):t]
    sequence = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    values = np.asarray(list(context) + [mask_id], dtype=np.int64)
    sequence[-len(values):] = values
    positive = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    position = int(np.flatnonzero(sequence != 0)[-1])
    positive[position] = history[t]
    return sequence, positive, probability

# Integrate into the supplied control's terminal sampler only.
# Preserve fixed 64/64 reconstruction/terminal branch allocation.
# R = summed reconstruction CE / valid reconstruction target count
# T = summed terminal CE / valid terminal target count
# loss = 0.5 * R + 0.5 * T
# Train one shared network per category; retain its single best checkpoint.
# Preserve the matching predictor writer and appended-MASK inference.

originality.positive: Fixing endpoint exposure while changing only conditional nonterminal sampling yields a precise, falsifiable BERT4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Masked terminal prediction and recency emphasis are established ingredients; the contribution is experimental precision.

future_potential.positive: An interpretable result can guide later temporal attention and content-specific modeling while preserving a simple deployment.
future_potential.negative: Effects may reflect context length or item exposure, and cannot establish compatibility or unresolved user needs.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention is localized to sampling and leaves architecture, checkpoint loading, and inference computation unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Matched randomness, accurate allocation definitions, explicit short-history handling, and separate diagnostic coverage require care.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item training for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone and masked prediction precedent for the proposed controlled sampling experiment.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal cutoff distribution for the pinned four-category task.
Masked-item prediction does not directly identify compatibility or fulfilled demand.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models pairwise historical time intervals within attention.
Motivates a later historical-gap bias experiment within the retained BERT4Rec backbone.
limitations: Transfer to bidirectional masked training requires explicit treatment of MASK temporal relations.
Provides no established gain under this task's pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: MARS: Attribute-aware representations and matching
contributions: Motivates attribute-sensitive representations and user–item matching.
Suggests jointly learned title and description features as a later single-network experiment.
limitations: Its pretrained-language-model setting does not validate a randomly initialized text encoder here.
Content similarity alone cannot establish functional complementarity or compatibility.
